clue.text: Players' timekeeper

parts.note: the players are musicians, and the device that keeps time for them ticks out the beat while they practise

explanation.definitionFit: A musician practising sets this ticking device to keep a steady tempo, so it keeps time for players.

clue.text: It goes wrong for the self-caterer

indicators.note: going wrong means the letters of the two words fall out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A self-catering holiday goes badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges IT GOES. The 'self-caterer' is not a holidaymaker cooking their own food but someone who caters only for their self.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfish person looks after only their own wants, catering for the self.

clue.text: Organised church circle in "Travellers' Rest"

parts.note: to run something is to organise it, past tense ran
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A church group is setting up a meeting at a pub called the Travellers' Rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish America a rancho was a rough hut or inn where travellers could put up for the night.

clue.text: Early invader having outlandish Roman name

indicators.note: outlandish means bizarre, so the letters of the word Roman are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: An ancient raider bearing a foreign-sounding Latin name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlandish' signals the anagram; 'Early invader' could suggest Romans or Vikings, but the clue's Roman is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans invaded England in 1066, early in its recorded history.

clue.text: This posting means trouble in China

indicators.note: in places the word for trouble inside the dynasty's name

parts.note: Ming was the Chinese dynasty, famous for its porcelain
to ail is to trouble, as an illness does

explanation.surface: A job posting abroad would mean trouble in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; China is the dynasty famous for porcelain. 'Posting' here is the sending of letters, not a job abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending items through the post is mailing them.

clue.text: Atoll explosion of real force

indicators.note: an explosion blasts things apart, so the letters of real force are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A Pacific atoll hit by a blast of real force, as in nuclear testing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion of' rearranges REAL FORCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped island built of coral around a lagoon.

clue.text: Bearer of grave words to Doctor Beryl, for example

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
beryl is a gemstone, so an example of a stone

explanation.surface: Words addressed to a doctor called Beryl.
explanation.walkthrough: Beryl looks like a woman's name but is the gemstone. 'Grave words' are an epitaph, the words on a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone carries the inscription over a grave.

clue.text: … delicate surgery, yet Dr isn't involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of the three words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Delicate surgery is going on, and yet the doctor is not taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges YET DR ISN'T. The leading dots tie the surface to the clue before, about a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Work on teeth and gums is a delicate branch of surgery.

clue.text: Knotty problem for patient without medicine

definitions.meaning: full of knots or knobbly swellings
a patient who has no medicine has ... to take, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Knobbly with knots is the botanical sense, and split into two words it says the patient has not a single measure of medicine.

clue.text: This locomotive has capital behind it

definitions.text: This locomotive has capital behind it

parts.words: This locomotive has capital behind it
parts.note: it reads like a well-funded engine, but means a service travelling away from London, so the capital lies behind it

explanation.walkthrough: British railways call a service heading away from London a 'down' one; 'capital' sounds like money but is the city.
explanation.definitionFit: On British lines trains leaving the capital run in the down direction, toward the provinces.

clue.text: Good opening with scope for clever move on board

indicators.note: the opening of the word Good is its first letter

parts.note: ambit means range or scope

explanation.surface: A good chess opening gives scope for a clever move later in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good opening' looks like the definition, a chess term; it gives only G.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess opening that sacrifices a piece for advantage is a calculated move on the board.

clue.text: One might have a wheeze and a peculiar stitch carrying mother

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the rearranged letters hold the word for mother
peculiar means odd, so the letters of stitch are put out of order

parts.note: MA is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone wheezing with an odd stitch while carrying their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' signals the anagram, giving STHTIC, and 'carrying' puts mother inside it; the first 'a' belongs to the definition, the second is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: People with this lung condition commonly wheeze when their airways narrow.

clue.text: Boxes for first-class prices?

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word class

parts.note: rates are charges or prices

explanation.surface: Boxes sent at first-class postage prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first-class' reads as top quality, but splits into an instruction: the first letter of 'class'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden packing cases are boxes.

clue.text: Speech meant to go round the world?

definitions.text: Speech meant to go round the world?

parts.words: Speech meant to go round the world?
parts.note: a language invented so that people of every nation could share it

explanation.definitionFit: Zamenhof built this artificial language in 1887 hoping it would become a universal second tongue.

clue.text: It is flung down-under and back

definitions.text: It is flung down-under and back

parts.words: It is flung down-under and back
parts.note: an Australian throwing stick that returns to the thrower

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down-under' means Australia; 'and back' says the thrown object returns.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved Aboriginal throwing stick is designed to fly back to whoever threw it.

clue.text: See frogman hide aquatic bird

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin
a diver is a water bird, the loon

explanation.surface: Look: the frogman hides from a water bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' just introduces the clue. 'hide' is not the verb but an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A frogman is an underwater swimmer wearing a wetsuit, a diver.

clue.text: Lager unconfined -— the time of one's life

indicators.note: unconfined means without its boundaries, so the outer letters of Lager are dropped

explanation.surface: Drinking lager without restraint, having the time of one's life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the time of one's life' sounds like a great party; it means how old one is.
explanation.definitionFit: Your years lived are the length of your life so far.

clue.text: Paintings of Hartung not hung

indicators.note: not hung tells us to take the letters spelling hung away

parts.note: the painter's name; the answer sitting inside it as a run is a coincidence, since the parse takes the letters of hung away
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pictures by the painter Hans Hartung that were never hung on a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Hartung was a French-German abstract painter; the gallery sense of 'hung' is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings collectively are works of fine creative craft.

clue.text: Self-esteem makes energy disappear

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
to go is to vanish or disappear

explanation.surface: Confidence that makes one's energy drain away.
explanation.definitionFit: One's sense of self-worth is the psychological self.

clue.text: Potter's Bar?

parts.note: the potter is a cue-sport player potting balls, and a bar to him is a ball placed to block his shot

explanation.walkthrough: Potters Bar is a town just north of London; here a 'potter' is a cue-sport player and a 'bar' is an obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving the cue ball blocked from the target ball bars the next player from potting.

clue.text: Gooch opening-less productive, but he can still clear the field

definitions.text: he can still clear the field

indicators.note: Gooch's opening is the first letter of his name

parts.note: lean means meagre or unproductive, so less productive is leaner

explanation.surface: The batsman Graham Gooch has a lean spell, but can still clear the field with his hitting.
explanation.walkthrough: Graham Gooch was an England cricket opener, so 'opening' fits him neatly. 'Clear the field' is not cricket but gathering leftover crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gathering grain left after harvest picks a field clean.

clue.text: Outworn inner pair

indicators.note: inner tells us to take letters from inside the word Outworn

explanation.surface: A worn-out inner pair, perhaps of socks.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a couple, a set of that number.

clue.text: West Riding paper variety of book cover

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Riding, a former division of Yorkshire

indicators.note: a variety of the word paper is its letters arranged in a different form

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire paper that comes in a book-cover version.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Riding was one of Yorkshire's three historic divisions. 'variety of' rearranges PAPER into APPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust jacket is the paper wrapped around a hardback.

clue.text: English miner looking odd in fur coat

indicators.note: looking odd means the letters of miner appear in a strange order

explanation.surface: An English coal miner looks out of place in a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking odd' rearranges MINER into RMINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The stoat's white winter pelt is a prized fur, worn on robes and coats.

clue.text: Noble sounding but without issue

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for a noble is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a baron is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A noble-sounding man who has no children to inherit.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no issue means childless, unable to bear offspring.

clue.text: Concomitants of chips, silicon, around army-site

indicators.note: around means the symbol for silicon goes round the word for an army site

parts.note: Si is the chemical symbol for silicon
a camp is a site where an army lodges

explanation.surface: Silicon chips made around an army base.
explanation.walkthrough: Silicon chips suggest computers; the chips are fried potatoes, and the answer is breaded prawns served with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded langoustines are a classic pub dish served with fried potatoes.

clue.text: King Charles's home ?

parts.note: the King Charles is a breed of spaniel, so its home is a dog house

explanation.definitionFit: A King Charles spaniel is a dog, and a dog lives in a small outdoor shelter.

clue.text: Into holidays abroad? I find there is still room

indicators.note: Into says the letter I goes inside the French word

parts.note: vacances is French for holidays

explanation.surface: Into holidays abroad? I find there are still places available.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel showing unfilled places has spare rooms.

clue.text: Far-off assistance for the windy condition

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters of far are put out of order

parts.note: aid means help or assistance

explanation.surface: Distant help for a breezy weather condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges FAR into AFR. 'Windy' is old slang for scared, not breezy.
explanation.definitionFit: Windy is British slang for nervous or frightened.

clue.text: Independently, fellows take time — and that's flat!

parts.note: apart means separately or independently
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Men taking time to do things on their own, and that is final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a flat statement; it is the home.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a set of rooms on one floor, a dwelling unit.

clue.text: Daisy's song-cycle ?

parts.note: the old music-hall song Daisy Bell is about a bicycle built for two, so its cycle seats two riders

explanation.walkthrough: A song cycle is a set of songs; here the cycle is a bicycle from the song 'Daisy Bell'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle with two seats, one behind the other, is the 'bicycle built for two' of the song.

clue.text: Law of nature said to attract interest

indicators.note: said tells us the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: money lent or saved, the principal, earns interest

explanation.surface: A natural law said to draw people's curiosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' looks like curiosity but is money earned on a loan's principal sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A fundamental rule of how nature works is a basic truth.
